title: C482/538/2023 of SOHEL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND THROUGH SECRETARY HOME, DEHRADUN

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
C482 No. 538 of 2023
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Raj Kumar Singh, Advocate, for the
applicant.
Mrs. Mamta Joshi, Brief Holder, for the State
of Uttarakhand.
The present applicant in this C-482
Application is the owner of the offending vehicle
bearing registration No.UK-07-TB-2757, being the
four-wheeler I-10. The said vehicle was said to be
involved in the commission of offence under
Sections 8/20/60 of the NDPS Act, which stood
registered by way of F.I.R. No. 25 of 2022, at
Police Station Mori, District Uttarkashi.
The grievance of the present applicant is, that
he had no role to play as such in the commission of
offence except for the fact, that he is the owner of
the vehicle and the accused, who were involved in
the commission of offence, are still languishing in
jail.
He submits, in case, if the said vehicle is kept
in the police custody, it will ultimately damage and
its cost will gradually diminish.
Hence, he filed a Release Application before
the Court of Special Sessions Judge, Uttarkashi,
seeking release of the vehicle. The same was
rejected by an order dated 1st February, 2023, on the
ground, that out of the two accused persons from
whom the recovery of 1 kg and 100 gm of charas
was made, since they are already languishing in jail,
and the vehicle, which was thus kept in custody,
was the case property, hence, it cannot be released
until and unless, the accused are released on bail.
Releasing of the accused persons on bail may
not be an exclusive ground to deny the release
application of the vehicle, which was allegedly
involved in the commission of offence because,

otherwise also, during the course of investigation,
and after submission of chargesheet, the details of
vehicle are already available with the police
authorities, and the same could very well be
retrieved from the present applicant, in an event, if
the vehicle is permitted to be released, to be
produced as and when required by the Court.
In the wider interest, particularly in order to
protect the vehicle from depleting, the vehicle in
question bearing registration No. UK-07-TB-2757,
presently lying in Police Station Mori, District
Uttarkashi, is hereby directed to be released, subject
to the condition, that the applicant furnishes a
surety of Rs. 3 lacs and further gives an
undertaking, by way of an affidavit, before the
Sessions Court concerned, that after the release of
the vehicle, he will not sell the same to a third
person, except with prior leave of the Court.
Subject to furnishing of said surety and
deposition of the security amount, and an
undertaking, the vehicle is directed to be released in
favor of present applicant.
Subject to the aforesaid, the C-482
Application stands disposed of.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
Dated 25.07.2023
Shiv
